disease_label_per_paper: Probable catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome with renal cortical necrosis, pulmonary embolism/infarction, hemolysis, and recurrent thrombotic events
presentation_summary: 40-year-old man was transferred for gross hematuria and decreased urine output after two weeks of chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, chills, and abdominal pain.
On admission he had severe headache, nausea, flank/back pain, creatinine 6.0 mg/dL, BUN 69 mg/dL, and MRI evidence of acute renal cortical necrosis.
Over three days he rapidly developed anemia, thrombocytopenia, and schistocytes, while lung perfusion scan showed right lower lobe perfusion defects suggesting pulmonary embolism.
Serology showed lupus anticoagulant and IgM anticardiolipin antibody; the paper classified the initial episode as probable CAPS.

risk_context.source_text_value: Fever and chills developed thereafter followed by abdominal pain.
neither intravenous heparin nor warfarin was used due to hemoptysis

observations.source_text_value: MRI of the kidney revealed acute cortical necrosis and azotemia progressed rapidly
lung perfusion scan revealed perfusion defects in the right lower lobe, suggesting pulmonary embolism

course_observations.source_text_value: In the course of 3 days, anemia ... with a hemoglobin level of 12.0 g/dL
Peripheral blood smear showed schistocytes suggesting hemolytic anemia
course_observations.quality_note: Exact fraction not reported; encoded as present at high qualitative activity.

imaging.source_text_value: Magnetic resonance imaging of the kidney revealed acute cortical necrosis.
perfusion defects in the right lower lobe, suggesting pulmonary embolism
Two months after the first attack, echocardiogram showed inferior and septal myocardial infarction
Chest computed tomography scans revealed both lower lobe pulmonary infarctions during later recurrence

serology.source_text_value: serologic results showed the presence of lupus anticoagulant
serologic results showed ... IgM anticardiolipin antibody

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Retrospectively, his clinical presentation fits into the category of probable catastrophic APS (CAPS).
presence of lupus anticoagulant and IgM anticardiolipin antibody

actual_treatment: anticoagulation withheld during initial episode due to hemoptysis
aspirin and clopidogrel after later myocardial infarction
long-term antithrombotic treatment started after later recurrence
quality_warnings: Lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibody are kept in serology/confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
Initial platelet count was high and the later collapse to 29 x 10^9/L is retained as course evidence rather than replacing the presentation value.
This case preserves bleeding/hemoptysis because it explains why anticoagulation was constrained.
